summary: A December 2025 complaint alleged that Fireflies.ai joined a Western Illinois Dreamers virtual meeting on 18 November after another participant enabled it, recorded Katelin Cruz’s speech, attributed statements to her and derived a voiceprint without her notice or written consent. The alleged biometric derivation and absence of adequate consent were never tried: Cruz voluntarily dismissed her suit without prejudice in March 2026. Separate 2026 Fireflies voiceprint cases were consolidated and contested, with a court ordering preservation of relevant recordings while a dismissal motion was pending. Fireflies’ current policy describes meeting recording and transcription but says personal information is not used to train AI models. No forensic voice template, exact meeting permissions, final liability or individual recovery is established here.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The complaint alleges that one participant’s activation was treated as authority to capture and process other participants’ speech without their consent; the facts remain untested after dismissal.

assessment_boundaries: The Cruz case was voluntarily dismissed without prejudice, with no merits determination.
Related Fricker/Martinez proceedings concern distinct participants and do not establish the specific Cruz event.
Speaker attribution or diarisation is not automatically proof of a retained biometric voiceprint; the complaint’s claim is disputed.
Fireflies currently denies personal-data training; no Otter-style model-training reuse is established here.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Cruz’s primary complaint identifies a specific 18 November 2025 Illinois meeting and alleges a participant-enabled Fireflies bot recorded, transcribed and attributed her speech, creating a voiceprint without written release. The court docket confirms her March 2026 voluntary dismissal without prejudice, not adjudication of those allegations. Later Fricker/Martinez docket activity concerns different plaintiffs and allegations; the court stayed discovery and expressly ordered preservation of recordings pending a dismissal motion. These proceedings corroborate an ongoing disputed product-level question but cannot prove Cruz’s claimed biometric template. Fireflies’ first-party policy confirms a recording/transcription purpose and states it does not use personal information for model training; that current assertion is not a forensic reconstruction of Cruz’s meeting. Whether Cruz received sufficient notice, whether a legally relevant voiceprint was generated, and any causal privacy harm remain unproven.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The pleaded governance boundary is the delegation of recording and voice-processing authority from a meeting organiser to every participant. The initial suit’s voluntary dismissal does not validate or refute the alleged meeting conduct, and ordinary speaker attribution does not prove a biometric template. There is no supported downstream training-reuse mechanism in this record.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This case is a dispute-bounded comparator for multi-party meeting authority. The product can capture meeting speech, but the unresolved question is whether each affected person’s processing authority was secured for the actual operation. Court procedural preservation of relevant recordings is an opportunity for future evidence, not itself proof of violation.
